title: Information
text: Information includes material in any form, including records, documents, memos, e-mails, opinions, advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, papers, samples, models and electronic data held by or under the control of a public authority.

title: Public Authority
text: Public authority covers authorities, bodies and institutions of self-government established or constituted by the Constitution, by law, or by government notification, together with the bodies and organisations covered by the Act.

title: Right to Information
text: The right to information includes inspection of work, documents and records; taking notes, extracts or certified copies; taking certified samples; and obtaining information in electronic or other prescribed forms.

title: Proactive Disclosure
text: Public authorities are required to publish specified organisational, decision-making, financial, procedural and other information and keep it updated at prescribed intervals.

title: Public Information Officers
text: Every public authority must designate Central or State Public Information Officers, as applicable, to receive and deal with requests for information and assist persons seeking information.

title: Request for Information
text: A person seeking information may make a written or electronic request in English, Hindi or the official language of the area to the Central or State Public Information Officer, with the prescribed fee.

title: No Reason Required
text: An applicant seeking information is not required to give reasons for requesting the information or provide personal details beyond those necessary for contacting the applicant.

title: Transfer to Another Public Authority
text: If the requested information is held by another public authority or is more closely connected with its functions, the application must be transferred within five days and the applicant informed.

title: Thirty-Day Response
text: The PIO must ordinarily provide the information or reject the request within thirty days of receipt. Where the information concerns the life or liberty of a person, the statutory period is forty-eight hours.

title: Deemed Refusal
text: Failure by the PIO to give a decision within the period specified under Section 7(1) is treated as a refusal of the request.

title: Additional Fee
text: Where additional fees are payable for supplying information, the PIO must communicate the calculation and particulars of the additional fee and the further information required for payment.

title: Fees for Information
text: Information under the Act is to be supplied on payment of the prescribed fee, subject to statutory provisions; persons below the poverty line are not charged the prescribed fees under the Act.

title: Information Free After Delay
text: When a public authority fails to comply with the statutory time requirement, the information is to be provided free of charge to the person requesting it.

title: Reasons for Rejection
text: When a request is rejected, the PIO must communicate the reasons for rejection, the period within which an appeal may be made, and details of the appellate authority.

title: Form of Information
text: Information should ordinarily be provided in the form requested unless doing so would disproportionately divert the resources of the public authority or be detrimental to the safety or preservation of the record.

title: Personal Information Exemption
text: The Act provides an exemption for information relating to personal information where the statutory conditions for the exemption are met, subject to the Act's public-interest and overriding provisions.

title: Complaint to Information Commission
text: A person may make a complaint to the Central or State Information Commission in circumstances specified by the Act, including inability to submit a request, failure to appoint a PIO, refusal to accept a request, or failure to receive a response.

title: First Appeal
text: A person who does not receive a decision within the statutory period or is aggrieved by a PIO decision may prefer a first appeal within thirty days to an officer senior in rank to the PIO in the relevant public authority.

title: Penalty on PIO
text: The Information Commission may impose the statutory penalty on a PIO for specified failures, including refusal without reasonable cause, failure to furnish information within time, mala fide denial, knowingly giving incorrect information, destroying requested information, or obstructing furnishing of information.
